set.descent_text: The route ends on the summit, so the walk-off starts at the top of the peak. From the top, follow the summit ridge east along the crest, tracking the cairns, until you reach the end of the last big buttress, where bolted anchors mark the first rappel; the station sits on the nose of the buttress and is easy to miss. Parties typically make two short rappels, and a single 60 m rope generally reaches the first. Below them, scramble down a gully, then work back across to a second gully and follow cairned third and fourth class ground through trees to the foot of the cliff. Avoid the big gully farther east, which is loose and harder than it appears.

set.descent_text: The route ends at the top of the First Buttress. From the top, which is close to the east ridge, head downhill along the cliff edge following cairns to chain anchors. One rappel of about 100 feet reaches ground that is safe to scramble. Follow cairns toward the low spot in the ridge, then take a faint path left; stay out of the obvious snow or scree gully ahead. At a small col, turn left and follow ledge systems down the lower First Buttress to the foot of Hallett Chimney.

Easy ramps and ledges left of the chimney lead up toward the white bands in the middle of the face, where the technical climbing begins. set.descent_text: The route climbs a tower on the left side of the upper First Buttress. A rappel from the top of the tower drops you at the foot of the rappels used by the east ridge descent. From there use that descent: follow cairns to the chain anchors, make one rappel of about 100 feet, and continue down the cairned ledges of the lower First Buttress to the foot of Hallett Chimney.

set.descent_text: The route tops out at a notch at the top of the Third Buttress, below the true summit. Immediately right of the top, a cairned third class gully leads west; go left of the tower and through the key notch, or you will cliff out. The gully is loose in places, so avoid it with others above. Near the bottom trend uphill and right to keep it gentle, then walk the talus back to the foot of the buttress.

set.descent_text: Scramble the airy second and third class ridge to the summit ridge. Then drop southwest to a pair of huge split boulders, cross the gully beyond them to grassy ledges, and wind down these to the big boulder where you stashed packs.
set.approach: Hike toward Lake Haiyaha from Bear Lake. Shortly before the lake, a climbers' trail leaves along the southeast shore and climbs talus. Work up a big snow patch that slants right, then traverse right to a massive boulder, about level with the foot of the climb; packs stay here. From it, head north on third class grassy ledges, bypass a talus patch, and cross one more third class band to the white and orange southeast face of the buttress. A ledge at the arete, with a fixed pin nearby, marks the start.
